dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: In the most ancient stories, Aramuhukunda had already left his mark.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Perhaps Aramuhukunda appeared first, then there were stories.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: In Aramuhukunda's own story, his enemies were Big Iron Chunks that could block out the sun and cut off rivers. There was also Marana that could turn Vana into Valuka.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: But Aramuhukunda and his partner Aradasha, together with the Golden Nara Varuna, defeated the monsters that Aranara could not defeat.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: However, after that, Aramuhukunda was just a story, and not in Vanarana anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Perhaps he went to a place far, far away with Nara Varuna.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Perhaps he is waiting for us in Sarva.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Perhaps he stepped alone on the path to facing the ruler of Valuka.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: #But because his story still exists, Aramuhukunda is still in Vanarana. The rivers know him, the trees know him, and even Nara {NICKNAME} now knows him.
